1._section_summary: This is a 'Data analysis' section describing the statistical methods used to analyze study data. The section details the use of IBM SPSS Statistics for descriptive and correlational analyses, including Pearson correlations between BMI, social safeness (SSPS), body appreciation (BAS-2), inflexible eating (IEQ), and disordered eating (EDE-Q). Path analyses were conducted using AMOS to examine whether the relationship between social belonging/safeness and disordered eating was mediated by body appreciation and inflexible eating, with BMI controlled as a confounding variable. 4._section_summary: This section presents path analysis results examining the relationships between social safeness, body appreciation (measured with BAS-2), inflexible eating, and eating disorder psychopathology. A fully saturated model with 20 parameters was initially tested, followed by a readjusted model with two non-significant paths removed. The readjusted model demonstrated excellent fit and revealed that social safeness had a direct effect on body appreciation (0.35), which in turn had direct effects on both inflexible eating (−0.35) and eating disorder examination scores (−0.32). The analysis also identified significant indirect effects of social safeness on eating psychopathology mediated through body appreciation and inflexible eating.
